subject: ZenHealth MSA: proposed compromise for excluded damages and mutuality
messages:

Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ZenHealth MSA redline - exclusion language and mutuality

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and came back with two asks that are blocking internal approval: first, they want the excluded damages language to be mutual (they want Redwood on the hook for the same categories of excluded loss), and second, they are asking for clarifying examples for what qualifies as consequential versus incidental loss. Claire is copied and will push a marked redline.

We attached the redline for your review (ZenHealth_MSA_redline_20280715.docx). On timing, we need to close financially by end of July to hit our onboarding milestone. Can we get a proposed compromise by COB Monday?

Appreciate it,

Molly Chen
Head of Partnerships
ZenHealth

Subject: Re: ZenHealth MSA redline - exclusion language and mutuality

Hi Molly,

Got the redline, thanks. Quick read-through below and sharing initial thoughts. Internal copy to Karthis (legal) for a fuller proposal.

Summary of asks from your redline:
- Make excluded loss / consequential exclusion mutual
- Add concrete examples of what sits in consequential/special/incidental/punitive
- Clarify interplay between exclusion and monetary cap

High-level: we are open to clarifying examples and tightening interplay language, but mutual exclusions are uncommon for us because they can create a carveout loop with our cap and insurance exposure. That said, there may be a narrow three-line compromise that preserves our cap while addressing ZenHealth's governance concern.

Action requested: Karthis, can you draft a short compromise text that: (1) keeps the overall liability cap intact, (2) maintains exclusion categories but makes them symmetric in scope, and (3) adds examples and an insurance-related exception? Ideally 2-3 sentences so we can share with ZenHealth this week.

Molly, we will get back to you with proposed wording by Monday COB. If there is a required escalation, please flag who on your side will sign off.

Thanks,

Rachel Kim
Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthis Legal <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Molly Chen <molly.chen@zenhealth.com>, Claire Hu <claire.hu@zenhealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ZenHealth MSA redline - exclusion language and mutuality

Rachel / team,

Thanks for looping me in. Below is a proposed compromise that balances ZenHealth's ask for mutuality with Redwood's need to retain an effective cap and avoid open-ended punitive exposure. I include rationale and a short illustrative example set.

Proposed compromise (to insert in Liability / Excluded Losses section):
1) Mutuality: Replace any one-way exclusion paragraph with the following: 
   'Neither party will be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, exemplary, punitive, or indirect damages, except as expressly provided in this Agreement.'

2) Interplay with cap: Add a cross-reference sentence: 
   'The foregoing exclusion of consequential and related categories is subject to the monetary liability cap set forth in Section X, and shall not be construed to expand the types of damages recoverable beyond those specifically enumerated in this Agreement.'

3) Examples and limited carve-ins: Add an examples paragraph: 
   'For clarity, the types of loss typically considered consequential or incidental include, without limitation, loss of profits, loss of business, loss of data, loss of reputation, and third-party claims for economic loss arising from interrupted services. Notwithstanding the foregoing exclusion, each party's liability for breach of confidentiality obligations, willful misconduct, or obligations to indemnify third parties for IP infringement shall remain subject to the monetary cap but not excluded by this paragraph.'

Rationale:
- Mutuality addresses ZenHealth's governance ask and reduces negotiation friction.
- The interplay sentence ensures the exclusion is not used to circumvent the cap or create new unlimited exposures for either party.
- Limited carve-ins (confidentiality, willful misconduct, IP indemnity) preserve recoveries that are market-standard and insurable.

Example scenario (illustrative):
- If an outage causes ZenHealth to lose customer revenue, that revenue loss would generally be excluded as consequential, but ZenHealth could still recover damages up to the cap for direct losses proved at trial, and for indemnified IP claims as set forth in the IP indemnity section.

Open points for sales/legal to decide before sending to ZenHealth:
- Whether to include 'exemplary' and 'punitive' in the mutual exclusion language or keep them carved out one-way only (our preference is to exclude those categories mutually because punitive damages are generally disfavored in contract law and may be hard to insure).
- Whether to add an explicit reference to 'insurance proceeds' or require each party to use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain insurance.

If everyone agrees, I can format exact redline language and return to Rachel to send to ZenHealth.

-Karthik
Director, Contracts and Commercial Law
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposed-exclusion-draft.txt (clean and redline versions)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthis Legal <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ZenHealth MSA redline - exclusion language and mutuality

Agree with Karthik's approach. A couple of tactical asks for the outbound note to ZenHealth:
- Keep the examples paragraph but mark it as non-exhaustive and for illustrative purposes only (helps avoid inadvertent expansion).
- On punitive/exemplary: we should keep them in the mutual exclusion but add a parenthetical noting 'to the extent permitted by applicable law' to avoid state-law anomalies.
- Ask their counsel for a single-sentence confirmation of signoff path if they need internal board approval; that will let sales know if we need to push pricing or PS timing.

If no objections, Karthis, can you produce the redline and a one-paragraph cover note to ZenHealth that Rachel can send? I want the cover note to be movement-oriented: call out compromises and remaining open points (punitive parenthetical and insurance confirmation).

Lauren Bishop
VP, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Molly Chen <molly.chen@zenhealth.com>, Claire Hu <claire.hu@zenhealth.com>

Date: 2028-07-19T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ZenHealth MSA redline - exclusion language and mutuality

Molly / Claire,

Thanks for the redline and for clarifying your team's priorities. Attached is a short compromise redline and a brief cover note. High level: we are willing to make the exclusion mutual and to add illustrative examples, provided we keep the contract monetary cap intact and preserve standard carve-ins for confidentiality, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity. We also added a parenthetical on punitive/exemplary damages that reads 'to the extent permitted by applicable law.'

Cover note (summary to include in email):
- We accepted mutual excluded damages language with illustrative examples to improve clarity.
- We cross-referenced the exclusion to the monetary cap so the parties remain subject to the agreed cap.
- We preserved recoveries for breach of confidentiality, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity.

Remaining items for your counsel:
1) Please confirm whether ZenHealth requires an explicit insurance covenant or whether your counsel is comfortable relying on the mutual exclusion plus the cap.
2) If ZenHealth's governance requires escalated approval for mutual exclusions, please let us know who will sign off and the expected timeline.

If Claire can confirm those two points, we are prepared to finalize the MSA and proceed to signature. We can also add a short SOW buffer if you need more time for onboarding.

Best,

Rachel Kim
Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
